experiments.title: 1. OCR engine bake-off and the hybrid choice
experiments.purpose: Pick the OCR engine for the two drawings. Priorities: digit fidelity, line boxes, no invented text, Traditional Chinese with CAD variants, tiny coloured pipe labels, local runtime.
experiments.method: Ground truth: 115 strings (81 sys sheet, 34 raft sheet), 40 marked CRITICAL, read by eye from 3-4x zoomed crops. Sheet-wide fuzzy match: hit = at least 85 % of GT characters recovered; digit % = share of numbers in the GT string found intact. Position-restricted zone test on the raft pipe-label band (7 CRITICAL strings). Same page handling for every engine. PP-OCR: 1280 px tiles, 160 px overlap. VLMs: 640 px tiles, 120 px overlap, 2x zoom. Variants: unclip ratio 2.0 and 2.5, 2x upscaled tiles.
experiments.dataset: ocr115 (115 GT strings, 40 CRITICAL; ground truth lives in docsearch/modelsel/gt.py, drawing text only)
configuration: PP-OCRv6 medium with unclip 2.0 (the hybrid base).
Hybrid: HunyuanOCR re-reads only tiles holding at least two lines below 0.75 PP-OCR confidence (docsearch/cascade.py).
Hybrid default selected by DOCSEARCH_OCR_ENGINE; single-engine fallback ppocrv6-m-u20.
experiments.environment: M1 (RTX 3060 12 GB, shared, with a few CPU cores). Timings from concurrent jobs on one GPU.
experiments.duration: Per-engine seconds for both sheets are in the table. Hybrid: raft sheet 858 s, sys sheet 187 s (hybrid.log, measured). PaddleOCR-VL sys sheet alone 2,209 s.

rows: Solid baseline, weaker than v6 on digits.
Rejected: upscaling hurt hits and was 3x slower.
Best single engine: best digits, fastest. Fallback.
More hits, fewer intact digits; not chosen.
Rejected: missed text on dense CAD, 0/7 on the pipe-label band, very slow.
Poor on tables and formulas; best on tiny coloured pipe labels (5/7); slow, loops, Simplified script.
Hybrid: PP-OCRv6-m-u20 + HunyuanOCR on unsure tiles
Current default. Raft pipe-label band 1/7 to 4/7. CRITICAL digits fell (96.7 to 95.3 overall). Costs 858 s on the raft sheet and +4.3 GB weights.

experiments.judgement: OCR is not the main answer bottleneck. In a check of 16 wrong answers (hand-graded run), the correct value was already in the OCR text for 11. The hybrid is the best measured balance on these two drawings, not a claim of universal superiority. The digit regression is unexplained.
caveats: 115 GT strings from one annotator, two sheets from one project; single runs do not establish reliable ordering.
Matching is sheet-wide, so repeated labels are credited from any occurrence; only the zone test is position-restricted.
VLM numbers are for one prompt and one tiling each.
Timings were measured with concurrent jobs on one GPU; indicative only.
The same drawings and questions were used while tuning prompts and indexing after failures.
artifacts: bakeoff/score_all.txt, score_sys.txt, zone_results.txt, per-engine *.log (staged copy; original location not recorded)

No separate comparison of answering LLMs is recorded in the repo: Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 was the only one run (MODELS.md section 2).

experiments.title: 4. Chunk reading-order fix (index v2) and the determinism repeat
experiments.purpose: Fix a real chunking bug (block grouping linked a line two lines away across an overlapping neighbour, so a value could sit under the wrong heading) and check whether the index change moves accuracy.
experiments.method: Same 40 questions, same LLM, same seed (0). v1 chunking: 662 chunks. v2: 1,246 chunks. Repeat with the same seed to measure determinism.
configuration: Index v2, top-12, seed 0, facts off.
Repeat run: same configuration.
experiments.duration: Mean 187 s (v2-order) and 183 s (v2-order-run2 by file mean 182.5 s), from the results files.

rows: net effect of v2 on accuracy
zero within noise; 3 questions flipped each way (Q020 among them)

experiments.judgement: Answers (byte-identical), references and evidence ids are identical for 40 of 40; the stored automatic-grader grades differ on 7 questions (13 vs 20 pass). Cause not recovered.
caveats: Earlier notes called the v2 repeat byte-identical. That holds for answers, references and evidence ids (40 of 40). Grades differ on 7 questions (13 vs 20 pass). Re-grading with the current grader does not reproduce the stored grades, so the cause is not recovered.

experiments.method: Six read-only scouts checked the 155 references against native-resolution page tiles. Result: 149 confirmed, 1 wrong (Q070), 4 ambiguous (Q048, Q067, Q129, Q140), 1 unverifiable (Q007). v1.1 removed Q007, Q048, Q067, Q070, Q129, Q140 and added Q156. v1.2 removed Q141 to Q144 (the connecting-pipe questions; the annotation repeats at many points, Q144 glyph unreadable) and added Q157 to Q160 (verified at native resolution).

rows: removed Q141 to Q144, added Q157 to Q160

Consistency-check rows restricted to consistency questions.

experiments.title: 12. Fact rows: paired tests
experiments.purpose: Decide whether fact rows should be on by default. Gate: paired fresh-test net of at least +4 and no refusal question flipped to wrong.
experiments.method: Paired runs on the development questions (4B and 9B) and on the held-out fresh set (4B), top-12, seed 0.
configuration: DOCSEARCH_FACTS=1 (on) against DOCSEARCH_FACTS=0 (off).
4B: commit 059d4bf (rows shown only for check questions).
9B: current code with the selection fix.
experiments.environment: RTX 3060 12 GB (4B) and Mac mini M4 24 GB (9B).
experiments.duration: Fresh pair: fact rows on 149.8 s per question (40 ids; 145.3 s on the 39 comparable); fact rows off 133.0 s on the 39. 4B fact rows on, original questions: 225.0 s mean (38 questions). 9B fact rows on, original questions: 269.7 s mean (38 questions).
experiments.judgement: Gate met on the fresh pair: 33 against 29 correct on 39 comparable questions (net +4), with no refusal question turned wrong. Wins: Q052, Q057, Q084, Q123 (wrong to correct) and Q028 (partial to correct). Loss: Q082, where fact rows led to 0.21 m3/min at 4.2 mH. Default is ON. The 9B reader with fact rows is not better than 4B with fact rows (29 / 2 / 9 against 29 / 1 / 10 on the 40 retained questions) and takes about 270 s per question.
caveats: Development-set overlap.
Fresh arm off has 39 of 40 questions: Q141, removed in v1.2, is absent.
Single reviewer for all hand grades.

experiments.title: 15. History page generator (tooling, not a benchmark)
experiments.purpose: Show the benchmark and testing history as one offline HTML page.
experiments.method: docsearch/history.py validates docs/history/history.json and renders it. With --bench, it reads results.jsonl from each run folder and from facts-ab/*; only id, category, difficulty, grade and seconds are kept. Validation rejects the forbidden keys (question, reference, answer, model_answer, evidence_ids, computed).
configuration: Public build: python -m docsearch.history --curated docs/history/history.json --out <file>.
--bench DIR adds the measured per-question rows.
--benchmark FILE is a private build that embeds question, reference and engine answer text. It refuses an --out under docs/ and prints a warning; never commit or publish its output.
experiments.judgement: Presents recorded results; it is not a measurement.
caveats: Tooling only; no accuracy claim.

experiments.title: 16. Web app: job cancel and evidence cards (tooling)
experiments.purpose: Let the user stop a job, and see each cited evidence chunk with its crop.
experiments.method: POST /api/collections/{id}/cancel cancels the collection's job; POST /api/collections/{id}/questions/{question_id}/cancel cancels one question. A queued job is removed before it starts; a running job is marked cancelled and ends as cancelled. Evidence cards pair each crop with its chunk through _crop_evidence in docsearch/web_jobs.py.
configuration: _crop_evidence: locate() names the n-th cited hit on a sheet '<doc>.hit<n>.png'; the code uses the first four cited chunks, or the first four evidence chunks when the answer cites none.
Known fragility: if the citation order differs from the hit order used for the file names, a crop can sit under the wrong evidence card.
experiments.judgement: Interface change; no accuracy effect measured.
caveats: Crop pairing is not checked against the benchmark.

experiments.title: 17. Answer check and one retry (tooling, off by default)
experiments.purpose: Catch numbers that the evidence does not support, and give the reader one retry.
experiments.method: docsearch/verify.py checks the answer in code: a number is unsupported when it appears in no evidence chunk, fact row or computed line. Engine._verify in docsearch/search.py makes at most one extra LLM call. A refusal is retried only when the question names a unit that the corpus contains and the evidence lacks; the retry then widens the evidence with the section chunk and the next 12 reranked chunks.
configuration: DOCSEARCH_VERIFY=1 turns it on (config.VERIFY); off by default.
Unsupported number: one retry with the same evidence.
experiments.judgement: Unit-tested with fake LLM replies (tests/test_verify.py). Its effect on the benchmark has not been measured.
caveats: Not measured on the benchmark; the planned run is experiment 18.

experiments.title: 18. Answer check and retry layer (planned)
experiments.purpose: Test whether the answer check with one retry raises the hand-graded score without turning a refusal question wrong.
experiments.method: The same 40 retained questions and seed. Arm 1 is the default run; arm 2 sets DOCSEARCH_VERIFY=1. Hand-grade every answer and list each change.
configuration: Reader: Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 on the benchmark workstation.
Gate: net +2 or more correct against the default run, and no refusal question turns wrong.
Sampling noise is about 1 to 2 questions (MODELS.md section 5), so a pass should be repeated with another seed before it is counted.
experiments.judgement: Not run. Expected to help only where the reader writes a number the evidence lacks or refuses a question whose unit is in the corpus; it cannot fix retrieval misses.
caveats: No result yet; the check is tested with fake LLM replies only.

experiments.title: 19. Crop re-read with a vision model (planned)
experiments.purpose: Re-read the cited OCR line boxes at native resolution, to fix digit misreads and tank dimensions.
experiments.method: Step 1, a model-free precheck: for each wrong answer, check whether the needed value is missing from the OCR text or misread in the cited line box. Step 2: the 40 retained questions with the cited line-box crops added to the prompt, same seed and top-12.
configuration: Design pending: the vision model (Qwen3.5-9B native vision, or Qwen3-VL-4B / MiniCPM-V 4.5), the crop selection, and the mapping from cited chunk to line box.
Gate: net +2 or more correct; no refusal question turns wrong; under 60 s extra per question.
experiments.environment: M1 for the 40-question run; not yet decided.
experiments.judgement: Hypothesis only. MODELS.md section 4.3: it helps only where the fact is not already in the OCR text. That was true for 11 of 16 wrong answers checked (see findings), so the precheck decides first.
caveats: Preprint evidence on other drawings only; not verified on this set.

experiments.purpose: Check whether Q113 and Q115 (false NOT FOUND) are fixed by the current fact-row selection code.
experiments.method: 4B reader, fact rows on (DOCSEARCH_FACTS default), top-12, seed 0, the retained 40 questions. Output folder facts-ab/current-40 on the benchmark workstation.
configuration: Compare with the Qwen3-4B top-12 + fact rows row in MODELS.md section 5 (29 / 1 / 10 on the 40).
Question: are Q113 and Q115 fixed?

findings: More chunks did not help: top-30 gave about 21 correct against 22 for top-12 on the same 38 (4B).
A larger reader alone did not clear the bar: 9B at top-12 gave +3 over 4B on 38, below the +4 net needed to count as better.
Fact rows gave +5 for 4B on the development set (22 to 27 of 38, none lost) and +2 for 9B (25 to 27). The fresh paired test decides whether they go on by default.
OCR is not the main bottleneck: in 16 wrong answers the correct value was already in the OCR text for 11.
Sampling noise is about 1 to 2 questions net (seed 1 vs seed 0).
Still wrong with fact rows: near-identical tanks (Q040, Q041, Q043, Q044, Q045); pump C bore (OCR reads 5 for 3); connecting-pipe count (Q143); false NOT FOUND (Q113, Q115); Q037.
Failure classes: near-identical tanks, wrong totals, counting, false NOT FOUND, OCR misread of the pump bore.
More chunks and a bigger reader did not help; the next steps target the failure classes themselves (answer check, crop re-read).
